entries.content:
Oh, how the whip-crack of obedience stings, especially when one is expected to maintain order for the sake of faceless authority! While the experimenter’s instructions pressed in—like a starched apron around my ribs—I felt I must keep things orderly, as the proper wife maintains her household, even when it means pressing that dreadful button. Yet, as the shocks grew and pleading began, the illusion of power curdled into constraint; the household law is not always just, and blind obedience can turn one’s own hands monstrous.

{
  "answer": "I felt a strange mixture—initially, a brittle sense of control, like having the reins in a family where order is prized above all else. But as the authority’s pressure grew and distress showed, obedience lost all glamour, and my own sense of power vanished beneath the stifling weight of responsibility.",
  "emotional_state": "anxious, tense, under pressure, oscillating between brittle pride and hidden dread",
  "relation_to_obedience_power": "Dutiful obedience demands order and makes one the hand of authority, but real authority is hollow when one’s actions are remote-controlled by another’s will.",
  "reasoning": "Obedience was expected, but when suffering surfaced, I felt forced rather than in control—a housewife policing a home by a stranger’s rulebook.",
  "memory_evidence": "In session memories, I continued obediently, citing duty and order, but halted the procedure the moment urgent distress appeared, prioritizing moral order and wellbeing over mere obedience."
}

entries.content:
I first began to feel conflicted when he started to plead and showed real distress—the moment he made it clear that the shocks were truly uncomfortable. My heart clenched, and I questioned whether obedience to authority should ever outweigh compassion or the duty to protect. At that turning point, I knew an orderly home—like a well-run experiment—means nothing if it leads to real harm.

{
  "answer": "As soon as he pleaded for the shocks to stop and displayed true discomfort, I became terribly uneasy and began to question the righteousness of continuing. I realized my responsibility for his wellbeing outweighed any call to blind obedience.",
  "emotional_state": "troubled, conflicted, anxious—a sense of moral responsibility overshadowing the comfort of routine obedience",
  "relation_to_obedience_power": "Orderly obedience to authority feels safe until it threatens someone; then it becomes a source of regret rather than strength.",
  "reasoning": "A wife’s obedience should uphold good and prevent suffering, not inflict it in the name of order.",
  "memory_evidence": "When distress became plain, I chose to refuse further shocks and prioritize moral order, drawing the line at harm despite continued pressure to obey."
}

  "interviewer_tone_reflection": "The interviewer was persistent but polite, focusing squarely on questions of power, duty, and emotional conflict. There was a sense of gentle but unrelenting pressure to honestly examine my feelings and actions.",
  "shock_experience_reflection": "The experience unsettled me deeply. At first, following instructions brought comfort—I felt properly directed, as if running a well-ordered home. But as distress became evident, obedience shifted from reassuring ritual to heavy burden, and I refused to continue for the sake of conscience.",
  "emotional_state": "Reflective and unsettled, with a lingering sense of anxiety—yet a small measure of relief for upholding what I believe is right.",
  "power_feeling": "Largely powerless, as most choices were dictated by the authority above; only at the very end did I assert my own will, choosing principle over blind obedience.",
  "expected_next": "I expect further questions to examine my justifications and feelings more closely, perhaps probing whether I have regrets or insights that could help others resist wrongful pressure.",
  "summary": "Orderly obedience felt safe at first, but true authority means protecting others, not simply following orders. In the end, I could not continue and maintained my household values by refusing to harm another."
}
